categoryNote: Individually selectable only; never emitted into a preset (presetExcluded is true on all 14 entries and is mechanically enforced by the generator). This file is the single source of truth for NX17. Design verdict: the category is deliberately mostly Defined/read-only. BCD is never written by code here because Microsoft's own BCDEdit reference warns that a /set can render the computer inoperable and that BitLocker/Secure Boot may need to be suspended first; the ReviOS negative-results ledger adds a concrete hardware regression (disabledynamictick broke ROG Ally sleep, r2). Per-device MSI and interrupt-affinity writes are Defined because the registry values are not documented public contracts and no device-stability gate exists in engine v0.1. HPET/platform-clock forcing is rejected outright; only detection and a removal-first symptom-gated procedure are defined. MMCSS-adjacent values (NX17-008/-009/-010), the Memory Manager legacy set (NX17-012) and PowerThrottling (NX17-013) are XREF/read-only so exactly one write path exists (NX03-007, NX05-007, NX03-006 respectively) and no duplicate registry target is declared. The one shipped write is NX17-011: a single documented ADMX-backed Windows Update driver-delivery policy value, journaled, consent-gated, idempotent and exactly reversible. No entry makes a performance claim; configuration intent and documented behavior only, outcomes PENDING until owner E2+ evidence.

tweaks.name: Timer resolution behavior
tweaks.description: Read-only report of timer-resolution facts (counter frequency, observed global-request value) with an honest explanation of why no machine-wide 1 ms timer is shipped.
tweaks.objective: Answer the timer-resolution question without shipping a contested, non-generalizable timer hack.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17TimerResolutionReport. The report returns the documented Stopwatch performance-counter frequency, the TimeSpan tick base, and the exact observed state (key/value existence, kind, data) of the community-established HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel :: GlobalTimerResolutionRequests value. It never writes that value and never presents a single current timer resolution as a machine-wide truth. WHY NO FORCING: since Windows 10 2004, timer-resolution requests are process/window scoped, so background processes do not inherit another process's request; a system-wide '1 ms' reading would therefore misrepresent reality (UltraOS finding, r4-synergy-ultraos.md, adopted by docs/RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION.md item 4-4). The reference ecosystem's own placebo list calls the '1 ms gaming timer' ritual folklore (r4), and FSOS-X had to rework its timer toggle specifically to handle global-request semantics (r1). No Microsoft page verified this session documents a supported global registry write that makes every process run on a fine timer, so the catalogue's EXPERIMENTAL/E0 classification stands and the entry is Defined: the report is the deliverable, not a timer change. OWNER GUIDANCE: if an application documents a per-process timer mechanism, use it in that application; do not bundle an unsigned timer-forcing utility (distribution hygiene, r4/r5). No performance claim is made anywhere in this entry; the report cannot prove that any timer value changes a game's frame pacing, and NEXTRIX does not assert that it does.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows manages timer resolution per requesting process/window family; no NEXTRIX value is written.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only timer-resolution report available on demand; no mutation is applied in engine v0.1.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17TimerResolutionReport returns readOnly=true, mutationSupported=false, a populated stopwatchFrequency, and the exact observed GlobalTimerResolutionRequests descriptor (present or absent). No journal entry and no mutation exist for this entry.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation is shipped. Nothing was changed, so there is nothing to restore.

originalState.method: Read-only capture of GlobalTimerResolutionRequests (key existence, value existence, kind, data) at report time; the report is not persisted and no mutation follows it.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
The report deliberately does not claim a global timer resolution: requests are process-scoped on supported builds.

tweaks.name: Dynamic Tick policy (BCD)
tweaks.description: Read-only capture of the disabledynamictick BCD element plus the exact, consented change and rollback procedure; no BCD write is automated.
tweaks.objective: Make the dynamic-tick question inspectable and reversible without letting the engine change boot configuration behind the owner's back.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17DynamicTickPolicy, which runs ONLY the read-only bcdedit /enum {current} form, parses the element table (ConvertFrom-Nx17BcdEnumText), and returns the disabledynamictick element's presence and exact value. THREE REASONS THE WRITE IS DEFINED, NOT SHIPPED. (1) Microsoft's BCDEdit /set reference states that disabledynamictick 'Enables and disables dynamic timer tick feature' but is an option that 'should only be used for debugging'; the same page warns that changing boot-entry options could render the computer inoperable and that BitLocker and Secure Boot may need to be disabled or suspended first. An automated writer that ignores BitLocker state is not acceptable. (2) Evidence of harm is concrete: ReviOS removed its own 'bcdedit /set disabledynamictick yes' with the in-code comment that it 'breaks ROG Ally sleep, see #167' (r2-atlasos-revios.md; COMPATIBILITY_RESEARCH section 3). Laptop/handheld sleep is a required function, not a metric. (3) Absence is not 'off': a stock element is usually absent, and a rollback must be bcdedit /deletevalue, not /set no. The report therefore distinguishes absent from present-with-value so an owner can record the exact prior state before any manual change. The requiredProcedure and rollback fields carry the full documented sequence: capture the enum line, verify BitLocker/Secure Boot implications, run exactly one /set or /deletevalue, restart, re-enumerate, and restore the captured state if sleep or resume regresses. No performance claim is made: disabling the dynamic tick changes timer-interrupt behavior on a platform-specific basis, and six reference projects disagree with no verified outcome (TWEAK_RESEARCH.md section 7).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default dynamic tick behavior; the disabledynamictick element is typically absent from the current boot entry.
tweaks.proposedState: Element state reported read-only (absent, Yes, or No) with the exact documented change/rollback procedure; nothing is written by NEXTRIX.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17DynamicTickPolicy returns bcdReadSucceeded with the parsed element state (present=false or present=true plus value), effectiveState, and the documented procedure. Verify any owner-performed change with bcdedit /enum {current}: the element must show the chosen value or be absent as intended.

rollback.procedure: No NEXTRIX-written state exists to roll back. For an owner-performed change: if the captured prior state was absent, run bcdedit /deletevalue {current} disabledynamictick; if it held a value, run bcdedit /set {current} disabledynamictick <exact prior value>; restart and re-verify.

originalState.method: Read-only bcdedit /enum {current} capture via Get-Nx17BcdElements; the report returns the exact element presence/value. An owner-performed change must journal that line before running /set.

sideEffects: If the owner applies disabledynamictick, sleep/resume behavior can regress on specific hardware (ROG Ally precedent, ReviOS #167); both directions carry risk.
The change requires a restart to take effect.
No performance outcome is claimed; platform timer behavior is hardware/firmware dependent.

tweaks.name: HPET policy (BCD)
tweaks.description: Symptom-gated detection of HPET/platform-clock overrides; arbitrary forcing and HPET-device disabling are rejected and never automated.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner evidence about clock-source overrides for a named symptom, without shipping the folkloric force-HPET/force-platform-tick change.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17HpetPolicy: read-only bcdedit /enum {current} for useplatformclock, useplatformtick and tscsyncpolicy, plus a read-only Get-PnpDevice presence/status check for the ACPI High Precision Event Timer (PNP0103). NOTHING IS FORCED. Microsoft documents useplatformclock as forcing the platform clock as the system performance counter and useplatformtick as forcing a platform-backed clock with no synthetic timers; both are marked 'should only be used for debugging'. The reference ecosystem disagrees in every direction - SapphireOS forces useplatformtick and disables the HPET device, while Vain and XOS delete the values instead - and no reference ships forcing as safe (TWEAK_CATALOGUE rejected list item 5; r1, r3). NEXTRIX therefore rejects both forcing and device disabling, and defines only a removal-first, symptom-gated procedure: capture the exact prior elements, name the reproducible symptom, remove an existing override (bcdedit /deletevalue) under owner supervision, restart and re-test, and restore the captured values if nothing improved. The report marks forcedSourcesPresent so an owner can see whether a third-party playbook left an override behind; it does not interpret that as a fault. No performance claim is made and 'HPET off' is never presented as a gain.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default clock-source selection; useplatformclock/useplatformtick are typically absent.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only detection of clock-source overrides and HPET device presence, with a removal-first, symptom-gated procedure; no forcing is applied.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17HpetPolicy returns forcingRejected=true, symptomGated=true, mutationSupported=false, the parsed useplatformclock/useplatformtick/tscsyncpolicy states and the HPET device probe state. After any owner-performed removal, bcdedit /enum {current} must no longer list the removed element and the named symptom must be re-tested.

rollback.procedure: No NEXTRIX-written state exists. For an owner-performed removal, restore the exact captured values with bcdedit /set {current} <element> <captured value>, then restart. Never disable the HPET device as a rollback or as a fix.

originalState.method: Read-only capture of the clock-related BCD elements and the HPET device's presence/status; the report returns them but persists nothing.

sideEffects: None in v0.1 (detection only).
If an owner removes a clock override, timing-sensitive software can behave differently; the change is only justified by a named symptom and is reversed from the captured state.
HPET device disabling is explicitly out of scope and is never offered.

tweaks.name: Platform clock source inspection
tweaks.description: Read-only report of the configured platform clock/tick source, the HPET device state, undocumented custom BCD elements and the counter frequency.
tweaks.objective: Provide trustworthy configuration evidence about clock-source selection without changing it.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17PlatformClockReport, a CORE read-only diagnostic. It merges: the current boot entry's useplatformclock, useplatformtick, disabledynamictick and tscsyncpolicy elements (bcdedit /enum {current}, parsed as text - no inference); the ACPI HPET device's presence/status via Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly; the documented Stopwatch performance-counter frequency; and a name-only list of any undocumented custom:* BCD elements present. selection is 'ForcedByBcd' only when a clock/tick override is explicitly Yes, otherwise 'WindowsDefaultSelection' - absence is reported as absence, never as 'off'. This distinction matters because Microsoft documents these as debugging options, not as supported tuning switches, and because a third-party playbook may have left an override behind. custom:* elements are flagged but never interpreted or modified: Atlas's custom:16000069 is documented by its own comment as undocumented (community source winaero.com), which is exactly the class NEXTRIX refuses to adopt (r2). No writes, no journal entries, no performance claim. The report is safe to run before and after any NX17 clock-related troubleshooting step.
tweaks.defaultState: Information only; Windows-selected clock source with no NEXTRIX values written.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17PlatformClockReport returns readOnly=true, mutationSupported=false, a selection classification, one state object per clock element (present/value/bcdRead), the HPET probe state, and any custom:* elements by name.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; nothing is changed.

originalState.method: Not applicable - the report IS the read-only state capture.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
bcdedit /enum and device enumeration can require elevation; a denied read is reported as readSucceeded=false rather than guessed.

tweaks.name: Curated BCD configuration set
tweaks.description: Read-only curated BCD report: one documented case (bootmenupolicy), per-entry approval required, no bulk writer and no undocumented elements.
tweaks.objective: Replace 'BCD optimization' bundles with a curated, individually approved, reversible definition - and ship no blanket writer.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17CuratedBcdConfiguration. The only curated case NEXTRIX defines is the documented bootmenupolicy element (Standard | Legacy), and even that is Defined rather than automated. Rationale: bootmenupolicy is a documented boot-menu presentation option, not a performance setting; a machine left on Legacy by a third-party playbook can be reported and, with explicit consent, restored to Standard using the documented procedure. Each would-be change requires its own captured prior state, its own approval event and its own rollback, so no 'optimize BCD' bulk action exists (directive; TWEAK_CATALOGUE). The report also reads the bootmgr timeout for context (information only - it is not offered as a change) and lists any custom:* elements by name. REJECTED EXAMPLES encoded in the report: bootstatuspolicy IgnoreAllFailures (suppresses boot-failure UX and automatic repair), custom:16000069 (undocumented spinning-animation element; Atlas's own comment cites winaero.com), and any multi-element blanket write. Microsoft's BCDEdit reference is explicit that /set can render the computer inoperable and that BitLocker/Secure Boot may need to be suspended, which is why even the documented case is owner-performed. No performance claim is made.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows-default boot menu policy (Standard on Windows 11) and default timeout; no NEXTRIX BCD values.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only report of bootmenupolicy, bootmgr timeout, undocumented elements and the single documented curated case with its consent procedure; nothing is written.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17CuratedBcdConfiguration returns bulkWriteSupported=false, perEntryApprovalNeeded=true, the current bootmenupolicy state, the bootmgr timeout state, any custom:* elements, one documented curated case and the rejected examples.

rollback.procedure: No NEXTRIX-written state exists. For an owner-performed bootmenupolicy change, restore the captured prior value with bcdedit /set {current} bootmenupolicy <Legacy|Standard>; if the element was absent, bcdedit /deletevalue {current} bootmenupolicy. Restart and re-enumerate.

originalState.method: Read-only bcdedit /enum {current} and {bootmgr} capture; the report returns the exact presence/value of each relevant element and persists nothing.

sideEffects: None in v0.1 (read-only report).
Any owner-performed BCD change risks boot configuration; Microsoft's inoperable-machine and BitLocker/Secure Boot cautions apply.
A boot-menu policy change is a presentation choice; it has no claimed performance effect.

tweaks.name: MSI mode per-device inspection & selective enable
tweaks.description: Per-device inventory of the MSISupported value with a value-presence gate; selective enable is Defined and per-instance only. Global MSI forcing is forbidden.
tweaks.objective: Expose which devices already expose an MSI switch without ever flipping a machine-wide switch or writing a value a device did not already have.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17MsiModeInventory over the shared read-only Get-Nx17PciInterruptInventory helper. For every present PCI device it reads, literal-path safe, HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\<instance>\Device Parameters\Interrupt Management\MessageSignaledInterruptProperties :: MSISupported together with the driver Service, and reports value presence, kind and data. A missing value is reported as 'not present', never as 0: the presence gate is the point (XOS's defensible variant, r1). GLOBAL MSI FORCING IS FORBIDDEN by directive and by TWEAK_CATALOGUE rejected list item 4; there is no all-devices option anywhere in this file. WHY SELECTIVE ENABLE IS DEFINED, NOT SHIPPED: MSISupported is not a documented public registry contract; enabling MSI changes interrupt delivery and needs a device restart or reboot plus an observation window for that device class; and engine v0.1 has no device-stability gate, so a failed placement could hang a storage or network device with no automatic recovery. The remediation path is defined precisely: select ONE instance whose value already exists, journal the exact per-device descriptor, change only that value, restart the device/reboot, observe stability, and restore the captured value (or delete it when it did not exist) on regression. The inventory also reports the affinity-policy key presence so the owner can see whether a third-party tool has already written interrupt policy. No performance claim is made: MSI is an interrupt-delivery mechanism, not a measured speed switch.
tweaks.defaultState: Per-device MSI support as exposed by the driver; MSISupported may be absent (not configurable through this value) or present as 0/1.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only per-device inventory; a selective enable is owner-performed for exactly one instance with its exact prior descriptor recorded.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17MsiModeInventory returns globalWriteSupported=false, perDeviceOnly=true, valuePresenceGated=true and one record per device with msiSupportedPresent plus the raw value. After an owner-performed change to one instance, re-read that instance's key and restart the device; the value must equal the chosen state.

rollback.procedure: No NEXTRIX-written state exists. For an owner-performed change, restore the exact captured per-device value, or delete MSISupported if it did not exist before; restart the device/reboot and re-read the key.

originalState.method: Read-only per-device capture of key existence, value existence, kind and data for MSISupported (and affinity values for visibility); the report persists nothing.

sideEffects: None in v0.1 (read-only inventory).
An owner-performed per-device MSI change can destabilise that device; a storage or network device may need recovery through Device Manager or Safe Mode.
No global MSI switch exists, so a device whose driver does not expose MSISupported is never modified.
documentationSource: research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (XOS enables MSI only where MSISupported already exists as 0/1, backs up each prior value to MsiModeBackup)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md rejected list item 4 (global MSI-mode forcing rejected; per-device only; XOS value-presence-gated approach is the only defensible variant)

tweaks.name: Interrupt affinity policy per-device
tweaks.description: Per-device, read-only inventory of interrupt affinity policy values; no write is shipped because the interface is undocumented and NX19 topology is not available.
tweaks.objective: Report per-device interrupt-affinity policy honestly and refuse to guess processor masks.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17InterruptAffinityInventory over the same read-only Get-Nx17PciInterruptInventory helper. It reports DevicePolicy, DevicePriority and AssignmentSetOverride presence/kind/raw value for each PCI device, plus the driver service and device identity, and it reports whether any NX19 topology function is loaded. NO WRITE IS SHIPPED, for three independent reasons. (1) These values are not documented public tuning contracts; Microsoft documents MSI/interrupt concepts for driver authors, not these per-device registry values as user configuration. (2) AssignmentSetOverride is a processor bitmask interpreted against the machine's processor groups; without derived topology a write is a guess, and NEXTRIX policy forbids hardcoded processor indexes (NX19 rule). (3) The reference ecosystem offers no defensible scripted implementation: XOS removes an Affinity Policy DevicePriority value as part of its MSI pass without documenting intent, and UltraOS ships Microsoft's GoInterruptPolicy as a manual tool with no scripted affinity logic (r1, r4). The entry is therefore read-only and topology-fed only through NX19's read-only interface: it reports whether Get-NxTopologyReport is loaded and refuses to choose processors without it. Affinity is kept distinct from CPU Sets (NX19 owns the CPU Sets path). No performance claim is made.
tweaks.defaultState: Per-device interrupt affinity policy as configured by Windows/driver/OEM; values may be absent.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only inventory of DevicePolicy/DevicePriority/AssignmentSetOverride with topology availability reported; no mutation is applied.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17InterruptAffinityInventory returns perDeviceOnly=true, mutationSupported=false, topologyFunction=Get-NxTopologyReport, topologyStatus (Available when NX19 is loaded, otherwise Unavailable), and one record per device with DevicePolicy/DevicePriority/AssignmentSetOverride presence and raw values.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation is shipped. Any future write must restore the exact per-device descriptor and be gated on NX19-derived topology.

originalState.method: Read-only per-device capture of the affinity-policy values and their kinds; the report persists nothing.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Raw affinity values are reported without interpretation because their meaning depends on undocumented semantics and processor groups.

research/sources/r4-synergy-ultraos.md (GoInterruptPolicy bundled as a manual tool; no scripted interrupt-affinity logic exists)

tweaks.name: System responsiveness value
tweaks.description: Read-only report of the documented MMCSS SystemResponsiveness value; the only write path is owned by NX03-007.
tweaks.objective: Make the machine-wide MMCSS responsiveness value visible in the advanced view without creating a second writer for the same registry target.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17SystemResponsivenessState, a read-only XREF to NX03-007 (MMCSS configuration). NX03-007 owns the single write path for HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile :: SystemResponsiveness; declaring a registry action here would be a duplicate modification target and a validator hard error, so this entry reports key/value existence, kind and data only. Microsoft documents the semantics: a REG_DWORD percentage of CPU resources guaranteed to low-priority tasks; values not evenly divisible by 10 round down; values below 10 or above 100 are clamped to 20; a value of 100 disables MMCSS (the driver returns STATUS_SERVER_DISABLED). The reference research records stock Windows 11 at 20 while several community playbooks write 10; NEXTRIX follows NX03-007's honest stance (stock value captured on the way in, ADVANCED, preset-excluded, no outcome asserted). This entry makes no performance claim: it records which policy is in force. Owners who want to change it must select NX03-007, which journals the exact original and applies the documented clamping semantics.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default SystemResponsiveness is typically 20 (reference research), or absent depending on image; policy value reported read-only.
tweaks.proposedState: Value reported read-only with documented semantics; any change is delegated to NX03-007 and is not performed by this entry.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17SystemResponsivenessState returns writeDelegated=true, ownerTweak=NX03-007, the key/value presence, kind and raw value. No journal entry and no mutation exist for NX17-008.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation is shipped. Rollback for a change belongs to NX03-007's journaled write.

originalState.method: Read-only capture of SystemResponsiveness (key existence, value existence, kind, data); nothing is persisted or written.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Changing SystemResponsiveness machine-wide is NX03-007's decision, not this entry's; the documented clamping and MMCSS-disable semantics apply there.

tweaks.name: Network throttling index
tweaks.description: Read-only report of NetworkThrottlingIndex with the honest scope note: it applies to MMCSS-tagged multimedia traffic only, not general network throughput.
tweaks.objective: Prevent the classic network-throttling tweak from being presented as general network tuning; expose its state without writing it.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17NetworkThrottlingState, a read-only observer of HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile :: NetworkThrottlingIndex. HONEST SCOPE: the value sits beside SystemResponsiveness and is community-known (XOS writes 10, r1), but Microsoft's MMCSS page verified this session documents MMCSS and SystemResponsiveness without documenting this value as a supported tuning contract. Its only asserted mechanism is throttling network packets for MMCSS-tagged multimedia traffic; it is not TCP window tuning, not a general download/streaming control, and not evidence of a game's network behavior. The catalogue's E0 classification stands. No NEXTRIX writer exists: NX03-007 owns the MMCSS value family and deliberately does not write this value, and NX17-009 does not either. NO PERFORMANCE CLAIM: a machine observed with a value of 10 is not 'misconfigured', and changing it is not asserted to improve anything. The entry exists so the advanced view can report the value and the scope note instead of silently shipping a broad claim.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows image value as observed (community references commonly see 10); read-only report, no NEXTRIX value.
tweaks.proposedState: Value reported read-only with the MMCSS-only scope note; no mutation is applied.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17NetworkThrottlingState returns mutationSupported=false, the key/value presence, kind and raw value, and the scopeNote stating that only MMCSS-tagged traffic is affected.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation is shipped.

originalState.method: Read-only capture of NetworkThrottlingIndex (key existence, value existence, kind, data); nothing is persisted or written.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
Reading a stock value is safe; interpreting it as a fault is not, because the value's scope is narrow and its provenance is community-established.

tweaks.name: Multimedia scheduler configuration
tweaks.description: Read-only composition view of the MMCSS service and existing task keys; NX03-007 owns every write.
tweaks.objective: Show the MMCSS surface in one advanced view without duplicating NX03-007's write path or inventing task keys.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17MultimediaSchedulerState. It reports read-only: whether the MMCSS service exists and its status/start type (Get-Service), and for each EXISTING task key under Multimedia\SystemProfile\Tasks the presence and raw values of Priority and Scheduling Category. It never creates a task key, never writes a value and never reconfigures the service (service ownership is NX11; disabling MMCSS would make every MMCSS value meaningless). XREF: NX03-007 owns the documented MMCSS write path, including SystemResponsiveness and opt-in per-task Priority (1-8; always treated as 2 for a High-category task) and Scheduling Category (High/Medium/Low). Microsoft documents GPU Priority and SFIO Priority as unused, and Clock Rate lost its guarantee in Windows 7; none of those is written anywhere in NEXTRIX, and this report does not surface them as candidates. The entry is a composition/report so the owner can see which tasks and values are in force, with no performance claim: MMCSS priority bands change how participating tasks compete for CPU, which is configuration intent, not a measured outcome.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows MMCSS service state and the stock task table (Audio, Capture, Distribution, Games, Playback, Pro Audio, Window Manager) with OEM additions.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only composition report of service state and existing task values; no mutation is applied.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17MultimediaSchedulerState returns writeDelegated=true, ownerTweak=NX03-007, the service state object, a task count and one record per existing task with Priority / Scheduling Category presence and raw values.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation is shipped. Rollback for a value change belongs to NX03-007's journaled write.

originalState.method: Read-only enumeration of the service state and existing MMCSS task values; the report persists nothing.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
The report enumerates existing keys only; it does not create, rename or remove any MMCSS task.

tweaks.name: Device installation restriction policy
tweaks.description: Applies the documented 'Do not include drivers with Windows Updates' policy (ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate), journaled and exactly reversible, with the driver-update workflow impact stated.
tweaks.objective: Offer one documented, narrowly scoped driver-delivery restriction for owners who deliberately manage drivers themselves - never as a default.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Set-Nx17DeviceInstallationPolicy, the only shipped write in NX17. It writes the documented ADMX-backed policy HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate :: ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate (REG_DWORD): 1 = Windows Update excludes Driver-classified updates in quality updates, 0 = allow them again. Microsoft documents the policy in the Policy CSP Update page ('Enable this policy to not include drivers with Windows quality updates'), with the Group Policy mapping 'Do not include drivers with Windows Updates' and the exact registry key/value name, which is why this entry is E1 while its scope is stated narrowly. SCOPE, HONESTLY: this restricts only the Windows Update driver-delivery path. It does not block manual driver installation, Device Manager, OEM updater applications, or driver packages delivered by other means. TRADE-OFF: new hardware may need a vendor-supplied driver instead of arriving automatically, and a device can remain on an older driver until the owner updates it. That is why the entry is ADVANCED, approval ExplicitConsent, presetExcluded and absent from every profile: the reject register condemns driver delivery blocked AS A DEFAULT (r1-r4), not an owner's explicit decision. EDITION: the CSP editions table lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT; the entry includes Home and flags enforcement as documentation-limited (the value is written and verified, but Home policy enforcement is not claimed). TRANSACTION: exact original descriptor captured (key existence, value existence, kind, data); an already-correct value journals a skip and is never rewritten; otherwise journal-first -> write -> read-back verify -> journal. A failed verification restores the exact original (or deletes the value if it never existed) and journals the failure. No performance claim is made.
tweaks.defaultState: Policy not configured: Windows Update includes updates with a Driver classification in quality updates.
tweaks.proposedState: ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate = DWord 1 (or 0 to restore automatic driver delivery), with the exact prior descriptor journaled.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState reads ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate back as DWord 1 after apply; the journal records one apply and one verify entry. Mode Default writes 0 and verifies the same way. The result states the workflow impact and the Home documentation-limited note.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the exact journaled original value/kind, or deletes the value if it never existed (policy-not-configured semantics). No restart is required; the next Windows Update scan evaluates the policy.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue records key existence, value existence, kind and exact data before mutation; the whole value is journaled before the write.

sideEffects: Windows Update stops offering Driver-classified updates in quality updates while the policy is active.
New hardware may require a vendor-supplied driver; manual installation and OEM updaters are unaffected.
Devices can remain on an older driver until the owner updates them deliberately.
No performance outcome is claimed.

tweaks.name: Memory Manager curated set
tweaks.description: Read-only report of a curated set of legacy Memory Management values; no write is shipped and mitigation values are out of scope.
tweaks.objective: Let an owner see which legacy memory knobs a third-party playbook left behind, without shipping undocumented memory 'optimizations'.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17MemoryManagerState, a read-only report over HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management for five named values only: LargeSystemCache (owned by NX05-007; its WMI mirror property exists but Microsoft marks it DEPRECATED/not supported), DisablePagingExecutive, DisablePageCombining, ClearPageFileAtShutdown and SecondLevelDataCache. Each is reported with presence, kind, raw value, owner and evidence label. NO WRITE IS SHIPPED, and no bulk set exists: the four non-NX05 values are legacy community knobs with no current Microsoft contract for Windows 11 client behavior, and their trade-offs are real (keeping kernel code/data resident reduces pageable memory; page combining is disabled; shutdown gets longer; cache sizing is a hint). The reference ecosystem sets DisablePagingExecutive/DisablePageCombining without verified benefit (r3), which is exactly the undocumented-benefit territory the catalogue flags; so this entry is TROUBLESHOOTING, individually approved and Defined. NX05-007 owns the only LargeSystemCache write; duplicating that target here would be a validator hard error, so the value is reported for visibility only. MITIGATION VALUES ARE OUT OF SCOPE: FeatureSettingsOverride and its Mask are banned registry targets in this key family (schema.json), and this report neither reads nor writes them; no mitigation mask is ever written anywhere in NX17. No performance claim is made.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows defaults / image state for the five named legacy values; read-only report.
tweaks.proposedState: Curated read-only report of the five values with owner/evidence labels and trade-off notes; no mutation is applied.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17MemoryManagerState returns mutationSupported=false and exactly five value records with presence/kind/value/owner; LargeSystemCache is labelled owner NX05-007 and no mitigation value appears.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation is shipped. Rollback for LargeSystemCache belongs to NX05-007's journaled write.

originalState.method: Read-only capture of the five named values (key existence, value existence, kind, data); nothing is persisted or written.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
The report exists to make legacy values visible, not to recommend them; the trade-off notes state the cost of each knob.

tweaks.name: Power throttling registry override
tweaks.description: Read-only report of the PowerThrottlingOff override; the only write path is owned by NX03-006.
tweaks.objective: Expose the EcoQoS/power-throttling override in the advanced view without a second writer or a second performance claim.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17PowerThrottlingState, a read-only XREF to NX03-006. NX03-006 owns the write of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerThrottling :: PowerThrottlingOff (DWord 1 disables power throttling, 0 restores default behavior) and already carries the honest provenance split: Microsoft documents the PowerThrottling key and the QoS/EcoQoS mechanism, but not this specific value name as a supported tuning contract, so the value-name provenance is community-established. This entry reports key/value existence, kind and raw value, and states the interpretation (1 = machine-wide throttling disabled, 0/absent = default). It never writes, never enables, and makes no performance claim: removing the OS lever that lowers background work's QoS class changes power/thermal behavior and interacts with hybrid scheduling hints, which is why NX03-006 excludes the battery-first profile P3 and never offers it to presets. A stock value is not a fault; the report exists so an owner can tell whether an override is active and where its rollback lives.
tweaks.defaultState: PowerThrottlingOff absent or 0 depending on the image (Windows default behavior); read-only report.
tweaks.proposedState: Override state reported read-only with interpretation and owner XREF; no mutation is applied.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17PowerThrottlingState returns writeDelegated=true, ownerTweak=NX03-006, key/value presence, kind, raw value and the interpretation string. No journal entry and no mutation exist for NX17-013.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation is shipped. Rollback for a change belongs to NX03-006's journaled write.

originalState.method: Read-only capture of PowerThrottlingOff (key existence, value existence, kind, data); nothing is persisted or written.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
An active override changes power/thermal behavior machine-wide; that decision and its exact rollback remain NX03-006's, not this report's.

tweaks.name: Driver Verifier diagnostic configuration
tweaks.description: Read-only Driver Verifier settings report with strict guardrails and a mandatory auto-clear procedure; enabling is never automated.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner a safe, evidence-based way to inspect and reason about Driver Verifier without turning a test tool into a shipped optimization.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implements Get-Nx17DriverVerifierState, which runs ONLY the read-only verifier /querysettings form. Driver Verifier is a diagnostic test mode, not a tuning feature: Microsoft's own page warns that running it can crash the computer, says to run it only on test/debug machines, and notes that selecting all drivers can exhaust special-pool/resource tracking and affect performance. NEXTRIX therefore NEVER enables it, never selects drivers, and never bundles a 'verifier on' switch. The report captures the exit code, whether settings appear to list drivers (a language-neutral .sys match, not a translation of localized prose), the listed driver names (capped) and the tool's own lines, with an explicit 'Unknown' sentinel when the query fails. STRICT GUARDRAILS (returned with every report): run only on a machine that can be rebooted/crashed; verify the smallest driver set that reproduces the symptom; set verifier /bootmode resetonbootfail BEFORE enabling so a failed start clears verification automatically; record the exact prior settings. MANDATORY AUTO-CLEAR (returned with every report): verifier /reset, restart, then re-check with /querysettings and /query; if the machine cannot boot with verification active, use the fail-safe boot mode or Windows Recovery to run verifier /reset. Owner-directed test mode only; no performance claim and no automated enable.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver Verifier not configured (or whatever an owner/OEM previously set); read-only report.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only settings report with guardrails and auto-clear procedure; no verification is enabled by NEXTRIX.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx17DriverVerifierState returns mutationSupported=false, querySucceeded/exitCode, listedDriverCount and settingsActiveLikely (DriversListed | NoDriversListed | Unknown), plus the guardrails and auto-clear procedure. After an owner-directed test, verifier /querysettings must show no settings once verifier /reset and a restart are complete.

rollback.procedure: No NEXTRIX-enable exists. Mandatory owner procedure to clear a test: verifier /reset, restart, and confirm with verifier /querysettings and verifier /query. Fail-safe: set verifier /bootmode resetonbootfail before enabling, or use Windows Recovery to run verifier /reset if the machine cannot boot.

originalState.method: Read-only capture of the current verifier settings (verifier /querysettings) and its exit code; no settings are changed and nothing is persisted.

sideEffects: None in v0.1 (read-only report).
If an owner enables Driver Verifier out of band, the machine may bug-check/crash and may need recovery; that is why enabling is not automated and the auto-clear procedure is mandatory.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devtest/driver-verifier ('Running Driver Verifier could cause the computer to crash'; test machines only; all-drivers caveat; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devtest/verifier-command-line (/querysettings, /reset, /bootmode resetonbootfail semantics and return codes; fetched 2026-11-23)
